concepts.note: They mix space and time between inertial frames while leaving the speed of light invariant.
concepts.title: Lorentz transformations

concepts.note: Events simultaneous in one inertial frame need not be simultaneous in another.
concepts.title: Relativity of simultaneity

concepts.note: All inertial observers measure the same vacuum speed c, independent of source motion.
concepts.title: Constancy of light speed

concepts.note: Velocities combine as (u + v)/(1 + uv/c²), so no inertial frame reaches c.
concepts.title: Relativistic velocity addition

subtopics.note: Physics is the same in all inertial frames and the vacuum speed of light c is invariant, so simultaneity and lengths become frame-dependent. The Lorentz factor is γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²).
subtopics.title: Special relativity

concepts.note: A particle at rest has energy E₀ = mc², even with zero momentum.
concepts.title: Rest energy

concepts.note: Momentum p = γmv preserves conservation laws at speeds near c.
concepts.title: Relativistic momentum

concepts.note: Binding energy lowers a system's mass by Δm = E_b/c².
concepts.title: Mass defect

subtopics.note: Mass is a form of energy, with a body at rest having energy E₀ = mc². Mass defects in bound systems therefore appear as released energy.
subtopics.title: Mass-energy equivalence

concepts.note: Position, momentum and current combine into Lorentz-covariant four-vectors.
concepts.title: Four-vectors

concepts.note: The causal structure separates timelike, lightlike and spacelike intervals.
concepts.title: Light cone

concepts.note: A particle's history is a curve through four-dimensional spacetime.
concepts.title: World line

concepts.note: Events are plotted with time versus spatial axes to display causal relations.
concepts.title: Spacetime diagram

subtopics.note: Space and time are unified into a four-dimensional spacetime with invariant interval s² = c²t² − x² − y² − z². This geometric formulation made Lorentz covariance manifest.
subtopics.title: Minkowski spacetime

concepts.note: Local free fall is indistinguishable from inertial motion, motivating curved spacetime.
concepts.title: Equivalence principle

concepts.note: They relate spacetime curvature to energy-momentum via Rμν − ½R gμν = 8πG Tμν/c⁴.
concepts.title: Einstein field equations

concepts.note: Free particles follow extremal proper-time paths, d²xμ/dτ² + Γμ_αβ dxα/dτ dxβ/dτ = 0.
concepts.title: Geodesic equation

concepts.note: Clocks deeper in a gravitational potential run slower than clocks higher up.
concepts.title: Gravitational time dilation

subtopics.note: Gravity is the curvature of spacetime sourced by stress-energy, and free bodies follow geodesics. The field equations are Rμν − ½R gμν = 8πG Tμν/c⁴.
subtopics.title: General relativity

concepts.note: The horizon radius is r_s = 2GM/c², proportional to the mass.
concepts.title: Schwarzschild radius

concepts.note: It is a null surface from inside which no signal can escape to infinity.
concepts.title: Event horizon

concepts.note: The spherically symmetric vacuum solution is unique and static, even during spherical collapse.
concepts.title: Birkhoff's theorem

concepts.note: A mass compressed within its Schwarzschild radius forms a region cut off from outside observers.
concepts.title: Black hole

subtopics.note: The first exact vacuum solution of Einstein's equations describes a static spherically symmetric mass and reveals an event horizon at r_s = 2GM/c². Its line element is ds² = −(1 − r_s/r)c²dt² + (1 − r_s/r)⁻¹dr² + r²(dθ² + sin²θ dφ²).
subtopics.title: Schwarzschild solution

concepts.note: Starlight grazing the Sun is deflected by δ = 4GM/(c²b), twice the Newtonian value.
concepts.title: Light deflection

concepts.note: General relativity explained Mercury's anomalous perihelion advance of about 43 arcseconds per century.
concepts.title: Perihelion precession

concepts.note: Radar signals passing near a massive body arrive later because of spacetime curvature.
concepts.title: Shapiro time delay

concepts.note: Orbiting gyroscopes measured geodetic and frame-dragging precession around Earth.
concepts.title: Gravity Probe B

subtopics.note: Eddington and Dyson's 1919 eclipse observations confirmed Einstein's predicted light deflection, the first of many precision tests. The deflection is δ = 4GM/(c²b) for impact parameter b.
subtopics.title: Tests of general relativity

concepts.note: The first direct detection came from two black holes merging about 1.3 billion light-years away.
concepts.title: GW150914 detection

concepts.note: The inspiral, merger and ringdown produced a chirp matching general-relativistic waveform templates.
concepts.title: Binary black hole merger

concepts.note: Kilometre-scale Michelson interferometers detect differential arm-length changes below 10⁻¹⁸ m.
concepts.title: LIGO interferometers

concepts.note: The dimensionless strain h = ΔL/L encodes the wave's amplitude and polarisation.
concepts.title: Gravitational-wave strain

subtopics.note: Accelerating masses radiate ripples in spacetime, predicted by Einstein in 1916 and first detected directly by LIGO on 14 September 2015. The strain h = ΔL/L measures fractional stretching of space.
subtopics.title: Gravitational waves
